title: Arsenal v Borussia Dortmund: Wasteful Arsenal Held to a 1-1 Draw
body:
Arsenal had to settle for a 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League, and once again they were punished for failing to convert their chances [S1]. It is the second game in a row in which their finishing has cost them [S1].

Maximilian Beier was the Dortmund player who secured the draw [S1]. Arsenal also have a selection headache, because goalkeeper David Raya will miss Tuesday's game with a shoulder injury [S2]. The early word is more reassuring, as BBC Sport reported that the injury will not require an operation [S2].

The wider picture is more encouraging. In their last five league matches, Arsenal have won four, drawn one and lost none, collecting 13 points from 7 goals scored and 2 conceded [ST1]. A run like that suggests a side that is winning games, not one that is falling apart. The problem looks like sharpness in front of goal rather than a lack of quality.

This was the kind of game that tells you more about character than tactics. The side showed enough resilience to avoid defeat, but the manager will know that a draw built on missed opportunities is not a performance to celebrate.

The Touchline Take: a point apiece and nobody fully satisfied, but the form says the sharpness is more likely to return than to vanish.
